Don't mind the playtime as I left for dinner so the real game was only 5 hours long before I got to the credits. Spoilers ahead. [b][h1]The Good[/h1][/b] [list] [*]You get to play as team Natsu. [*]You get to meet other characters and if you meet them enough times they give you their card to call in battle. [*]It uses a fail forward mechanic so you also unlock stuff the more you play with leveling up being fast. [*]Team combat is unique and the game uses a system that doesn't rely on card draw to okay effect. [*]Animations for attacks are cool if it's your first time seeing them (however, I'm fairly certain I've seen them from a gatcha game I've played before) [/list] [b][h1]Cons IP wise[/h1][/b] [list] [*]In all of Fairy Tail, you only get to play as 5 characters. [*]Remember all those amazing antagonist and guild members? You don't fight any of them. [*]Enemies look like they belong in a FF game or were bought from some asset pack. [*]No voice actors. [/list] [b][h1]Cons Game wise[/h1][/b] [list] [*]EXTREMELY RNG Reliant. Characters get a RNGed skill book that you go to the dungeon to get points to level up and if you manage to beat the run that character is saved for the team dungeons. [*]You cannot edit the decks of the characters you saved. Whatever you cleared the above with you are stuck with so if you wanted to change your team you need to rebuild fresh and hope your skill book isn't trash. [*]There's only 3 dungeons. [*]They reuse boss sprites for regular encounters. [*]The "final" fight is just a of hp sponges with high damage. [*]Mechanics are limited. There's no burn damage for Natsu, no Freeze for Gray etc. [*]Cards don't have upgraded version. When you enchant them they get a random buff and you have no list of what they can be. [*]Discarding is really weird. You select the cards you want to keep in hand by selecting them and hitting the redraw button which removes the nonhighlighted ones. [*]Comboing means getting 2 specific cards to play in a specific order. However, as the book is RNG you might not get a combo or a good one. Even if you did get a combo there's no guarantee you'll find those cards to fit in your deck. [*]Team combat is unbalanced. Enemies are from the 1 person dungeon with maybe a boss you fought before slightly stronger. [*]Team exploration is boring. You cannot get new cards, remove cards etc. so you are locked in that playstyle until the end game. [*]During Team Exploration even if you don't have a certain party member on the team you can still encounter their tomes during your run which makes no sense as you cannot switch party members mid game. [*]There are no relics during the team game which limits your playstyle even more. [/list] I can go on and on but at the end of the day unless you love the IP it's not going to entertain you for very long. Even if you are a fan, the novelty wears off fairly quick too. If it's on sale for 5 euros then sure go for it otherwise I'd recommend support Knock on the Coffin lid which has 30x the content and 50x the strategy.

[table] [tr] [td] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38553778-All-about-Strategy-Games/] Follow my Curator Page for more Strategy Games! [/url] [/td] [/tr] [/table] Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a rogue-lite deckbuilder. [h1]Story[/h1] You can easily play the game without knowing anything about fairy tail (like me) and still get the story. Sure, I imagine it could help to know the characters, back story, etc. but it seems like I still get what's going on. [h1]Labyrinths[/h1] Every run consists of three labyrinths. You have around 10 moves to make on the map till you fight the boss. There are normal battles, elite battles, a campfire, a shop, events, and lacrima. Lacrima is used to upgrade your character's abilities which are stored in a tome. After every run, you can save up your tome (up to four per character actually) to get into the next labyrinth with a saved tome. [h1]Battles[/h1] The game's battle mechanic is best described as Easy to learn, and hard to master. It's as simple as it could be. You get 4 cards per turn, can redraw one time for 5HP loss, and play up to three cards (every card costs mana and you have three to start out with). It really gets strategic when thinking about combinations, countering bosses, doing magic chains, etc. Some of these words sound complicated. Fear not. [h1]Tutorial[/h1] The tutorial is really good. They will literally explain everything to you in a short period of time. It's a short but detailed tutorial + there's a menu explaining keywords, etc. if you even need that. [h1]Meta Progression[/h1] The game is a rogue-lite and there's progression to be made. First off, you unlock new labyrinths, forwarding the story and increasing the difficulty. There's a resource called "LumYou also unlocks amulets and stuff, so there's that. The meta progression is really engaging since it progresses the whole game and you'll be able to fight with two or even three characters at the same time, allowing for even more strategic depth. [h1]Pros and Cons[/h1] + engaging thanks to the meta progression + impactful animations. I very much like them since they feel more alive and fun attacking with special attacks that even look hurtful. + easy to learn, hard to master. Even if you're not into deckbuilder but you're into the series: you can easily play and like this game. And if you're not into the series but love deckbuilders, this is for you, too. It can get really strategic in battles. + good music. Most of the time when playing deckbuilders I just mute the game and listen to music, but I do in fact like it in this game. + good performance. I did not have any problems playing the game on my desktop as well as on my laptop. I have not tried to play on my Steam deck yet. +- some boss battles can take quite a bit of time. This is neutral since some people like it and some don't. Personally, the "long" fights did not feel draining because I was already much into the fights at this point but I can imagine some people disliking this. It also depends on your strategy and how much you're willing to take (as in: how much HP loss) for battles to get longer. - I would like to unlock even more things like cards. - basic story. I did not need that really. - harder difficulties are missing. Don't get me wrong, I did NOT play through the whole game yet so maybe it's something I don't need in the end, or it's unlocked later, but I can imagine hardcore deckbuilding fans wanting even more of a challenge (Tho I don't think the game is easy and look at how many deckbuilders I've played). [h1]Conclusion[/h1] Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a highly addictive and strategic rogue-lite deckbuilder. It's easy to learn but hard to master. Even if you're not into the series but into deckbuilders, you'll easily grasp the basic story and love the battles as well as the progression. The animations add to the fun since they are impactful, short, and still fun to watch. There's plenty of stuff to like and I'm honest: I never thought this game would be so good since I thought it would be a short cash grab - but it's definitely not! You should definitely get it! So far, the game is incredibly unbalanced. When you get one upgrade, that upgrades Lucy's prayer from healing 4 to healing 5, and then have to fight a boss that one shot me at 37 health with no crit? On floor 2? That's literally not even fair. During my 2 hours, I got 6 runs in. 1 Natsu, 1 Gray, 4 Lucy. Lucy makes the most sense for me, and got me the farthest. The farthest being the boss of floor 2. Sometimes it's Mono Bird! Who's "hit with 6 cards or more" thing is bugged and never worked, even when I managed to use items and hit him for 8 cards! Meaning I always got hit with the big finisher attack! How great and awesome! I never got my "step foot in the labrynith" achievement, but I don't care about the bugs on the Steam achievements. I care about the game physically being unfun to play. Steam told me this would be like Inscryption. Except, in Inscryption Chapter 1, losing gives you rewards still. You can still easily get back to where you were and learn something from it. Chapter 2? Absolutely no downside to losing! You can try again and again with various methods. Chapter 3? A mix! You only lose your money and your spot. If you've already cleared the area of encounters, then you have nothing to worry about and just get to try again. But FT Dungeons? Has none of that. Everything you do gets reset, you keep nothing. You can't even go back after losing and collect say a pouch of the lacrima you had last round. There is no incentive to losing other than the "points system" which give you useless items or lore. I do not want to talk to Blue Pegasus members in the Labyrinth, I want a way to get past floor 2. When there's no incentive to losing and every incentive to winning in a game like this, it makes players more frustrated when you powercreep your literal tutorial levels. I'm not one to criticize without offering solutions. So 1. Give more healing items. Even with a bag full of them+Polyuscia's medicine, I die constantly due to just getting flat overpowered. 2. Give more ways to upgrade your cards. When you have a run that's expected to go super far and then you get 0 ways to upgrade things except the campfire at the end of a floor, which usually you HAVE to use for healing or just die immediately on the next floor, then there's no point in contnuing that run. Hell, without a reliable way to upgrade things then you have no use going past floor 1 at all. Because you will get crushed. 3. Rearrange some of the decks. I get that the whole point is that you have to explore to get more magic, but when Gray literally spawns with 2 cards and the rest are basic attacks that everyone has? It's just pathetic. And if you can't get chests to spawn or don't have enough fuel to even get to them, then you're stuck at a boss with almost nothing! 4. Keep the Book of Remembrance through all runs. Starting a run with +2 to say Lucy's Virgo Stardress is not going to kill replayability. It will help players who get far return to where they were and will help players who are struggling to get further actually manage to play your game. I want to love this game. I want to keep playing this game. Fairy Tail has a special place in my heart and it genuinely upsets me to see something I looked forward to buying be so ♥♥♥♥♥♥.

+ Nice to see Indie developer working on a major IP officially --- A big minus for me: Lack of Fairy Tale themed music, current music is not bad but totally lacked the Fairy Tail oomph. Would be nice if they let us use custom music.... + Many great design concepts... - but ruined by a rigid combo system that does not gel well for RNG-heavy roguelite, which broke the synergy for a potential good design (more below) - English translation of names and skills does not align to Anime/Manga. Lucy's keys/skills feel MTLed. - Very grindy to unlock anything and everything, including abilities -- Extra, Extra grindy: expectation is you keep running the labyrinth (first half of game) for each char multiple times until you can RNG a good skill compendium, which you can then use for the second half of the game -- Currently, Erza is crashing the game in deeper dungeon. - No access to library during game play, hard to keep track of what's what and what you are missing. ++ Well Priced for an IP title. Games are way overpriced these days and this is not one of them, which is my main reason for picking this up. The labyrinth portion of the game (1st half) let you grow each character individually and learn skills (good idea). Skills are learned based on RNG card drops. The skill pool is also RNG and you can re-randomize the unused portion with a "Mazefruit" (nothing wrong so far). However, we are given very limited # of turns on each floor to power up... 1) Combo skills locked behind RNG skill grid (no issue by itself but...) 2) RNG on skills so you might not get the required skills for the combo you are able to RNG unlock 3) Higher tier skills cost 2 or 3 energy to use. Your default energy is 3... so making those 4 points combo unusable by default. You also need to get lucky on a RNG card mod to lower cost on one of the cards. The crux is the current combo system can be unwieldy unless RNG god favors you. Roguelite is not an excuse to turn this into an exercise of frustration in the 2nd part of the game. This is just poor execution Dev needs to rework the combo system to make it more relevant for RNG nature of the game. Or if they want to keep the current fixed skill combination, the skill grid is not the right place for it. Unfortunately there are more - than + at this point in time, so I would not recommend it until they optimize game play and fix the crashing bugs (or Erza smacking down on the devs :P)

It pains me so much to have to leave negative review. But after the long wait of this major patch, the core logic flaw in the endless dungeon is still unfixed...the endless dungeon should be the end game for player to enjoy but.. all I get is frustration and not joy. I loved this game and I played so many hours in it, the following flaws have been there ever since release, but still dev still cant get it right. Endless Dungeon Flaw [A] Monster scales way faster than player, player have to choose between few resources ( get new card, enchant card, upgrade card's level (new function), rest, or shards to passive ability), with these many choices, you are not guaranteed to get what you want (yes roguelike), but what you get is not enough to face the enemies and bosses. -If you pick new card , you only have 3 mana, getting 1 cost card = no damage, getting 2 cost card = you might left with 1 mana every turn, getting 3 cost card = useless because it doesnt do enough, 3 cost AOE cant wipe the map -if you choose to enchant, you get no rest = no hp, enchant doenst even help much -upgrading the card = stuck with original deck forever -get shards = unlock Unison Raid = need NEW cards -get Single Target = facing Groups of monsters -get AOE Card = not enough damage [B] With this resource problem already heavy enough, 2nd level you get a teammate, and they share the resource! The new teammate always stuck with basic attack only because you cant even make it in time to build Main character. [C] With 2 teammates trying to fight for resource, the Boss Skill is insane, they require you to maybe do 100 damage but guess what? TOO EARLY to be able to do 2 damage, okay we try the buff strategy but guess what? THEY nerfed the ♥♥♥♥ outta Wendy's heal and buff, Grey's block , and added TONS of debuff from Enemy and Boss [D] Mirajane shouldnt have to take a turn to get outta Satan Soul...she is already hard enough to control I DO LOVE THIS GAME FOR REAL, I love fairy tail and I do think the devs did a fantastic job show casing the character's uniqueness, but seriously the core flaw is seriously severe...

首先，先肯定一波，在一众拉稀拉出狗屎的妖尾游戏里面，一款能玩的现代rogelike游戏肯定是非常强大的。 ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 但是。你这数据计算的方式未免太逆天了。 我玩这么多年的游戏没见过这样的。 +10暴击，+10暴击，我应该得到一个+20的暴击吧？ 怎么他妈的到你这变成了两个独立的+10暴击呢？你用你哪个器官想出来的这玩意你告诉我？脚心吗？ 你要是设计成这坨样子你当他不存在就完了呗。我草 为什么艾露莎还拿暴击当特色的，温蒂还用闪避当特色的？哪来的脸？ 叠半天一下都触发不了，我都乐了。你可真行。 ------------------------------------------------------ 再说说你这魔法联动系统................ 策划你小子是不是沉迷过天外武林，怎么就这么精准的把天外武林的糟粕给送进来了呢？？？？？？？？ 一开始卡池比较小也就算了，有的人物TM的一开始卡池就巨大无比，这个系统简直是约等于不存在了。 而且吧.........怎么联动完了就是千篇一律的加伤害呢，还不如天外武林呢 ------------------------------------------------------ 总结，这策划将就像是蜥蜴人，靠着模仿肉鸽游戏勉强终于做出来了不是狗屎的一款妖尾游戏。但是 我感觉他并没有理解到底什么是肉鸽游戏，逆天的匪夷所思的设定到处乱飞，完全不参考同类竞品的处理方式。真感人（）

豪丸！这两天等级终于打到100级了，特此留念。（这几天貌似更新了不少内容，我看游戏里新添了什么祈祷、浮空之类的新机制，暂时还没体验。以下都是基于本人10月17号之前的游戏经历得出的主观结论） 我个人平时卡牌肉鸽类的游戏玩的少，可能给不出什么专业性很强的见解。但作为一个追了妖尾十几年的粉丝，FAIRY TAIL 地下迷城真的是一个很棒的作品（而且最近也在持续更新，据说还有新的魔法卡以及任务追加，看得出作者的用心程度）。在游戏中，你可以使用出绝大多数原作出现过的技能，甚至百年任务的技能也有做进去！！！！！！谁懂啊，第一次在妖尾相关的游戏里看到了融合星灵衣，差点激动到昏厥（） 稍微分享一些游戏心得吧~ 1.治疗类的技能感觉略鸡肋。一夜的那个治疗技能只提供幽默的3点群体治疗，温蒂的治疗技能也只有在凑魔法联动的时候还能有点用。真的很生草啊，我玩到后面唯一一个用治疗技能的角色竟然是露西，手牌凑满3张星灵魔法卡就能提供10点群抬，勉强能说的过去（）。这个游戏比较关键的机制我感觉是闪避和额外能量，真的是可以产生质变。 2.结合我的游戏体验以及个人偏见，我认为强度排名是：温蒂≥露西＞纳兹＞格雷＞＞艾露莎（对不起艾姐，但我真的觉得你好难用呜呜呜呜呜呜呜，要是有人会用艾露莎还请教教我TAT)。组队打架的时候就纳兹+露西+温蒂，群体增伤+龙之力秒人，boss都可以三回合秒掉（） 护符的话我个人比较喜欢带影龙+阿库诺洛基亚（就那个开场能量+1的）+主角团大魔导演武服（就是给角色专属卡牌的那个护肤）+其他（比如冥宫龙的记忆、100级解锁的体力+100、露西的水瓶座星灵衣，温蒂的白月等等） 3.先说温蒂吧。超绝群体buff+闪避+偶尔比肩纳兹的超高爆发伤害。我感觉这个游戏，闪避真的是很重要的机制。一个60%闪避挂上去就能水灵灵地避开很多致命伤害（特别是到了后期有的boss a你一下就是几十上百的伤害，偶尔躲掉一两个真的是质变。明星单卡：①钢腕之力：超绝群体增伤+超绝魔法联动，钢碗配天空甲矢的伤害谁用谁知道。②疾驰之风：闪避真的很好用很好用！！！有时候逆天改命就靠闪避了。要是不喜欢赌博的话还是请老老实实温蒂+露西+格雷叠盾玩吧。③白月：高贵的免费卡片，也有一些很不错的魔法联动配合。④天空的波[风?]（最后一个字我不会念）:aoe伤害配减伤，个人建议配合附魔魔力-1服用。⑤照破天空穿：超绝灭龙奥义懂的都懂，打输出用的。⑥神的骑士：群体增伤，温蒂的核心机制。⑦龙之力：灭龙魔导士的独有机制，无条件伤害×2给予了温蒂和纳兹超高上限的输出空间，建议配合额外能量使用。个人常用小连招：龙之力+钢腕之力+天空甲矢，一回合伤害100+轻轻松松，要是有影龙支援技能or天空甲矢与天空乙矢的魔法联动伤害更高。⑦天空乙矢：队里有温蒂的情况下，要是在地牢里看到雪莉娅会直接送天空乙矢卡片和魔法联动技能。 4.露西：啊啊啊啊啊啊啊啊啊，作为妖尾里我最喜欢的角色，我对露西的爱也是一如既往带进了游戏中。露西的技能风格是整个游戏里最丰富的（很符合星灵魔导师的职业特点，多面手在任何场合都有一定的发挥）。先说优点：闪避+丰富的打断技能+全面的辅助能力+bug级别的水瓶座星灵衣和双子座星灵衣，使得露西小天使几乎可以承担所有工作，甚至输出有时候也不必纳兹他们低。明星单卡：①打断类的黄道十二宫钥匙：露西核心机制，在游戏后期打断地方的一个行动往往能起到决定性的作用。②双子座星灵衣：看到也有朋友对这张卡大家赞扬，说他是最强铜卡真的一点也不过分。闪避+追击技能，仅仅只需要1点能量。追击这个技能在很多情况下都是附魔的优选项之一（额外增伤+快速过牌），双子座星灵衣就这么水灵灵的直接给你了，有时候我会攒2~3张双子座星灵衣卡片，打起架来丝滑不少。③水瓶座星灵衣：1点能量即可得到高额aoe伤害+高额增伤+情怀，使得露西也可以获得比肩纳兹温蒂的输出能力。我个人也是比较喜欢囤2~3张。④水瓶座钥匙：情怀加成+高额aoe输出+群体打断，附魔的时候选消耗-1会更加舒服~⑤天蝎座钥匙+星灵衣：后期很舒服的魔法联动，无条件打断+附加闪避，以及天蝎座星灵衣和水瓶座星灵衣也有魔法联动，使用下来体验很好。⑥白羊座钥匙+星灵衣：评论区有dalao开发出了格雷+温蒂+露西的叠防御流打法，群体减伤+叠盾可以为团队提供很好的保命作用。⑦星图史话、合体星灵衣、妖精之球：这三个放一起说好了。超绝情怀加持，不低的伤害+强力辅助效果，看到就是必选好吧。你都玩露西了，不放放大绝招心里过意得去嘛~（水瓶座相关技能也是同理） 5.纳兹：纳兹我就简单说说吧。很多卡输出都很不错，不过核心卡主要还是：龙之力，雷炎龙模式，炎龙王模式，七炎龙的力量。我发现游戏作者真的很懂诶，像这种玩家看到就会血液沸腾的技能就会做得非常厉害（露西的水瓶座、合体星灵衣、星图史话、妖精之球也是同理），这个游戏你要是想打出爆发伤害真的很需要额外能量+高费卡减费。在温蒂的辅助以及额外能量的加持下，纳兹是可以做到一回合300+的爆发输出的。 I hate to write negative reviews for small studios, but this game says it's a deck-building rogue-like game, but it doesn't feel as such when you play it. For starters - card mechanics are fairly shallow. You only get to play up to 4 cards per turn, and the only thing you can do with these is to discard some to re-draw once. It helps to be mindful about cards that are left in your deck, but there are no mechanics that enable meaningful deck interaction, like card draw or selection, you have to hope to draw a right piece for the most part (you can't even keep a card to play it next turn). The primary synergy this game is built around is to play cards in pairs for a combo effect - that is pretty much the extent of it. The only real deckbuilding mechanic here is the deck bloat - by taking too many cards you decrease chance to draw a right pair, but again all available play around that is rather primitive. Combat mechanic is fairly shallow too. A cool concept here is that every character has a certain theme going about them - like converting blocks into attacks, or stacking up crit chance, or buffing/debuffing enemies, which is great on paper. In reality, because you have so little resources to work with, most of the time you spend either attacking and stacking block. I'm not even sure it's possible to do a build where you'd burn or poison all opponents to death while dodging their attacks just because there are not enough cards to support this interaction, most of cards I've seen just do damage with different side-effects. But the cardinal sin of this game is how you select cards. Usually in deck building games you get to chose one card from a pool every now and then, so you can build a deck around a certain theme. In this game, after every battle you're presented with 3 rewards - usually XP, an item (or a buff), and a card. So the only choice you have is to whether to pick that card, or not. I can't understand why. They have a brilliant idea that you first complete a dungeon with every character individually, building a deck for them, and then these characters team up with their selected decks, which should in theory allow you to be smart about synergies in your team. In reality though, because of how little control you have over cards you pick, it's almost impossible to force any particular archetype, so it feels like you're playing a roulette. I don't see myself grinding the starting dungeon 10 times, hoping that a right combination of cards would pop up. I did have fun for my 8 hours of play though. Battles are dynamic, music is energetic, characters make flashy attacks and look really cool while doing so and you do have to use your brain every now and then. It is the lack of replayability that warrants the negative review. I don't see any reason to do it again - there weren't any cool card interactions that would make me go "wow, I need to try and build around that". I didn't know anything about Fairy Tail universe, and I still don't after completing the game, because there is no storytelling or character development here. The game plays like a remastered jrpg from SNES era, except there is nothing but battles and abilities your characters have are assigned to you randomly every turn from a pool you've built. And there are other pixel-art jrpgs that also look great and have rouge-like mechanics, but with a proper depth - like Star Renegades for example, which is the one I recommend.

游戏玩法还行。但整个游戏平衡和数值给的很烂。特别是闪避，暴击，还有对面怪的数值，生存力，以及费用这块。这些我觉得都得推翻重做。游戏闪避暴击啥的数值给的非常保守，都是10%或20%，还有回合限定，大概率还闪不过，哪怕是闪也只能闪一次，闪完一次，整个buff就消失了，可以说面对多动怪或者被围殴一个闪根本没多大用。暴击更是影响计算，因为这游戏三星难度怪伤害非常高，压根不敢去赌伤害会不会暴击一次打死，多的卡不敢指其他怪，而不多又怕不暴击一次带不走。而且游戏有时候会出一些粪怪遭遇战，比如三四个哥布林，全出攻击，每个攻击都十多点，防御一张才七防，起两张防不住一个平a，每次碰到那种几个小怪全出攻几乎都得掉一层皮。更难绷的是这游戏没有稳定加费用上限的办法，只能靠触发被动。很多卡基本都是二费，大多数时候一回合只能打两张卡，要么防了没攻要么攻了没防。卡牌联动效果我觉得就不应该要自己点出来，卡牌联动就该直接特定卡联动，而且联动卡也只是加输出威力，压根没其他作用。最后只是一场数值对撞游戏，要么先把对面秒了，要么就被对面秒了。后面地牢也是纯粹靠叠数值，辅助根本没法玩，没伤害被怪灌伤害灌死。 开局选遗物，有些初始遗物根本就是凑数的，明明可以角色自带，费用拆出来到初始选遗物占格子，用途太有限了。实在不行直接做个局外成长都比这强。。随机事件甚至还带概率。 还是看看大更新会不会做一些调整目前来说实在是爽又爽不起来，策略也没啥策略，全靠运气。

FAIRY TAIL DUNGEONS is a creative blend of roguelike exploration and deck-building strategy that takes the beloved Fairy Tail universe in a different direction from traditional anime RPG adaptations. Developed by Ginolabo and published by Kodansha, the game focuses less on recreating major story arcs and more on delivering a replayable tactical experience where players guide familiar guild members through dangerous dungeons filled with enemies, rewards, and unpredictable challenges. The result is a compact but engaging adventure that successfully combines the appeal of collectible card mechanics with the charm of the Fairy Tail franchise. At the heart of the game is its card-based combat system. Rather than relying on action-oriented battles, every encounter revolves around building and utilizing a deck of cards that represent magical abilities, attacks, and character-specific techniques. Each turn requires thoughtful planning as players manage resources, chain together powerful effects, and adapt to changing situations. The strategic depth grows steadily as new cards are unlocked, encouraging experimentation and rewarding players who discover effective combinations. Fans of deck-building games will find plenty to enjoy, while Fairy Tail enthusiasts will appreciate seeing iconic powers translated into tactical gameplay mechanics. The roguelike structure gives the adventure much of its replay value. Dungeon layouts, enemy encounters, and rewards vary from run to run, ensuring that each attempt feels somewhat different. Players are constantly faced with decisions about which path to take, which cards to add, and how much risk they are willing to accept for potentially greater rewards. This design keeps the experience engaging even after multiple playthroughs, as success depends on both strategic deck construction and the ability to adapt to unexpected circumstances. One of the game's strongest qualities is how it captures the spirit of its source material despite its relatively simple scope. The characters retain their recognizable identities, and their abilities reflect the powers fans know from the manga and anime. Building a deck around a specific character's strengths creates a sense of ownership and connection that helps the game feel authentically tied to the Fairy Tail universe. While the narrative takes a back seat to gameplay, the familiar cast and magical themes ensure that the franchise's personality remains present throughout the adventure. Visually, FAIRY TAIL DUNGEONS adopts a colorful anime-inspired style that suits the series well. Character illustrations are attractive and faithful to their original designs, while magical attacks are accompanied by effects that add excitement to battles without becoming visually overwhelming. The user interface is easy to navigate, allowing players to focus on strategy rather than wrestling with complicated menus. Although the production values are modest compared to larger licensed releases, the presentation remains polished and appealing. The progression system further enhances the experience by giving players long-term goals beyond individual dungeon runs. Unlockable content and new strategic options provide a satisfying sense of growth, making failures feel less discouraging since each attempt contributes to future success. This approach fits perfectly with the roguelike formula and encourages players to continue refining their tactics and exploring new playstyles. The game does have a few limitations. Players hoping for an extensive story-driven RPG may be disappointed by the relatively light narrative content. The focus is clearly on gameplay systems rather than character development or plot progression. Additionally, while the randomized structure adds replayability, some players may eventually wish for more environmental variety, additional characters, or a broader range of gameplay modes to extend the experience further. The game's smaller scale occasionally becomes apparent during longer sessions. Despite these shortcomings, FAIRY TAIL DUNGEONS succeeds as an entertaining and thoughtfully designed spin-off. It takes a familiar franchise and places it within a genre that complements its magical combat and diverse cast surprisingly well. The combination of strategic card battles, roguelike progression, and recognizable Fairy Tail elements creates an experience that feels fresh while still respecting its source material. Whether approached as a fan of the anime or as a player who enjoys deck-building adventures, the game offers enough depth and replayability to justify multiple runs through its dungeons. Rating: 8/10

Bored and disappointed. Good bones, bad execution. System seems fun at first, but horribly inefficient UI for a card game causing tedious slow gameplay. It makes the party system annoying. Icons for cards aren't intelligent enough to help memorize them, aka by color coding and other hints that imply certain effects. To make it worse, what should be a fun system where you plan a party (3 different decks) is a total pain. You must build and save each deck by playing a 1-character game, on the easiest floor, for every character, before you can team up. Not only is that annoying in general, but this means you have to awkwardly tiptoe around the fact each character has to solo to make their deck when in reality you are going to end up a party later and should be able to plan for synergy. And then congrats, you have 1 deck per character. If you want a different deck or to adjust it, you have to again run the beginning of the game and save that deck for later use. Random problems: - Horribly easy. I am good at card games, but I'm 8 hours in and have not ONCE felt like I was in danger. Even though it's probably hard later, the badly designed UI and lack of QOL features would make the min-maxing needed very annoying. - Occasional terrible communication about effects or how stuff works. Was there a weak translation team maybe? - Annoying flashing every second of battle that lights up the room. This pisses my dog off and it also pisses me off. There is no option to reduce it. - Cannot speed up unnecessarily slow flashy attack animations. - Unusual disparity in pixel art quality. Backgrounds are meh, characters are meh, but then the enemies and bosses suddenly obviously took 10x as much effort.

At this point, just rename them DoT and call it a day, they could've made each statuses unique Magic chain, although cool, is very restrictive, most if not all the time you can only select very specific cards to be the trigger (like it has to cost 1 AP), this limits the builds you can make significantly Verdict 8/10, fun for a while until it gets stale due to the cons mentioned, but for its price, you can't complain much, it's a solid game

Fairy tail setting is also a nice thing - I'm not the biggest fan and I don't know some of endgame bosses' origin but it didn't felt forced at all (unlike many other anime/film games). The only thing is I wish some card's and characters would be more balanced - I suspect devs don't have enough testing data to act on this because game is somewhat niche but I hope one day they will fix the numbers.
